# MM-P1-L4-CN01 Maintenance manual - Heat Treat CNC turning center #1

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-CN01

Scope
This maintenance manual covers preventive and corrective maintenance tasks for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 identified as EQ-P1-L4-CN01. It describes the tools required, the recommended procedure for warm-up, chuck jaw bolt torque verification, inspection points relevant to heat treat production, and the acceptance criteria for return to service. This manual is intended for qualified maintenance technicians assigned to P1-L4 and for use in coordination with operating procedures. Consult related documents MM-P1-L4-CN01-S2, SB-1046, and SOP-P1-L4-01 for complementary electrical, safety bulletin, and operator-level instructions.

Background and rationale
EQ-P1-L4-CN01 operates in a heat treat cell and components are exposed to thermal cycling. Proper warm-up prevents thermal shock to bearings and spindle seals and stabilizes dimensions before machining critical features. Correct chuck jaw bolt torque secures workholding and reduces the risk of jaw slippage or part ejection during turning operations. The values specified in this manual reflect OEM recommendations and plant validation for stable production and safety.

Tools
- Torque wrench capable of applying and holding the specified torque for chuck jaw bolts; use the torque head recommended by the tool supplier.  
- Socket or bit compatible with chuck jaw bolt heads specified on EQ-P1-L4-CN01.  
- Infrared thermometer or surface temperature indicator for non-contact verification of spindle housing temperature.  
- Clean, lint-free rags and approved solvent for degreasing contact faces.  
- Permanent maintenance log or electronic maintenance record entry device for documentation.  
- Personal protective equipment as required by SOP-P1-L4-01 and SB-1046.

Procedure
Overview: Perform operations in a controlled sequence to warm the spindle, inspect, set chuck jaw bolt torque, and record results. Follow lockout/tagout and machine-specific safety checks in SOP-P1-L4-01 before starting any mechanical work.

Warm-up
Begin warm-up with the machine powered and in a safe condition for unattended spindle rotation per SOP-P1-L4-01. Run the spindle through a progressive ramp to operating speed to bring bearings and seals to thermal equilibrium. Maintain continuous rotation for the spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 15 minutes to achieve dimensional stability and reduce the risk of concentricity error once heavy cuts begin. Use the infrared thermometer to verify uniform warming of the spindle housing; allow the warm-up routine to complete fully before proceeding to clamp verification.

Inspection
After warm-up, perform a visual inspection of the chuck, jaws, and surrounding guard. Clean all mating surfaces and remove swarf and debris from the chuck throat. Inspect jaw threads and bolt heads for signs of galling, wear, or corrosion. If damage is suspected, escalate per the corrective maintenance flow in MM-P1-L4-CN01-S2.

Torque verification and adjustment
Ensure the chuck is in the safe maintenance position and that power and motion state comply with SOP-P1-L4-01 controls for securing tooling. Using the torque wrench, verify and, if required, tighten the chuck jaw bolts to the chuck jaw bolt torque for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 90 N·m. Apply torque in a star pattern across the jaw bolts to distribute clamp load evenly and to avoid inducing uneven stress. If bolts repeatedly lose torque or show signs of thread stripping, remove the jaw assembly and follow the component repair procedure in MM-P1-L4-CN01-S2.

Examples and special cases
- Example: For a workpiece showing axial runout after initial clamping, re-run the warm-up routine and re-verify the chuck jaw bolt torque for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 90 N·m before attempting further corrections.  
- Example: If the spindle feels rough during warm-up, stop the machine and follow inspection checklist in SB-1046 before resuming. Do not proceed to production until mechanical integrity is confirmed.

Records to keep
Maintain a maintenance entry for each action taken. Each record must include the following fields: equipment id, maintenance technician identifier, reason for maintenance, actions performed (including notation that the spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 15 minutes was completed), torque values observed and applied with notation that the chuck jaw bolt torque for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 90 N·m was used, any parts replaced or escalated, and references to related documents cited in this manual. Store logs in the plant maintenance record system and attach any relevant photos or torque wrench calibration stickers per SB-1046.

Acceptance criteria
Return to service is allowed only when all of the following are confirmed:
- Visual inspection shows no damage or excessive wear to chuck jaws, jaw bolts, or mating surfaces.  
- Warm-up procedure completed and documented indicating the spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 15 minutes was performed.  
- All jaw bolts verified and set to the chuck jaw bolt torque for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 90 N·m and torque wrench readings recorded.  
- No abnormal noise or vibration observed during a monitored run at machine idle and during a no-load spindle acceleration as defined in SOP-P1-L4-01.  
- Maintenance entries and any required escalation actions recorded and accessible alongside MM-P1-L4-CN01-S2 and SB-1046 references.

Related documents
MM-P1-L4-CN01-S2  
SB-1046  
SOP-P1-L4-01
